notes: Health axis (T-DEEPSEEK-115): LockoutTracker::health reports every dispatch scope as a typed susi_core::model_health::ModelHealth — Healthy/Unhealthy{RateLimited} honouring Retry-After/Degraded/Unhealthy{ServiceError}/Dead{InvalidCredential|Unsupported|InsufficientQuota} — and run_jobs surfaces JobOutcome::target_health on the production dispatch path; capability ranking is structurally unaffected by availability storms (refutation-tested). Arbitration axis (T-DEEPSEEK-116): crates/susi-gemi/src/key_arbitration.rs is a process-global KeyArbiter enforcing per-key concurrency (default 4), a sliding per-key request-rate window (default 60/min), and a global in-flight ceiling (default 32), overridable via SUSI_KEY_ARBITRATION_*. Every production provider.generate call in susi-gemi admits through it: the failover cascade try_providers (engines/runtime.rs) skips a saturated key and tries the next provider, and all four one-shot probe helpers (coding_models_ext, frontier_ext, open_weight_ext, openrouter_ext) refuse on denial. Scope = registered provider name, which carries exactly one credential — the key pool. Honest limits: arbitration is process-global inside the daemon (external agent CLI subprocesses arbitrate in their own process; provider-side limits remain the backstop); the legacy susi-gawd model_rate_arbitration and susi-gawd-swarm parallel_admission/Shared::with_admission remain test-only machinery on the unreached swarm parallel-dispatch stack; susi-gawd-swarm cloud_recovery's direct provider.generate is not production-reached so it bypasses nothing in practice.
